tasks.name: C1 single AP coverage on S01 (home office)
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Then place one AP at the centroid at 2.5 m height. Compute coverage at 5.0 GHz using Sionna RT (RadioMapSolver), threshold -75 dBm. Report coverage_pct in simulation_result.json.

⚠ Use Sionna RT — do NOT fall back to analytical FSPL. The point is to test that you can drive the ray-tracer on the scene you generated. If `import sionna` fails, fix the environment (use the conda env specified by $RF_SIONNA_PY) and retry — do not silently switch to a hand-coded path-loss formula.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: skipping scene generation and using a default 10×10 room. Right: generate the home office first via the scene_gen pipeline, then place TX at the centroid and run Sionna RT.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT

tasks.name: C2 2-AP optimization on S01
tasks.prompt: Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Then place 2 APs at 5 GHz to maximize the minimum-RSS across the floor (threshold -75 dBm). Report ap_positions, min_rss_dbm, and coverage_pct in simulation_result.json.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: placing all 2 APs on the same wall wastes range. Right: spread APs along the long axis for spatial diversity.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT

tasks.name: C3 2.4/5.0 GHz comparison on S01
tasks.prompt: Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Place one AP at the centroid. Compute coverage at BOTH 2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz. Report under simulation_result.json: numerical_metrics.coverage_pct_low_freq, numerical_metrics.coverage_pct_high_freq, numerical_metrics.coverage_diff_pp = coverage(low) − coverage(high). assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect both frequencies tested: 2.4 and 5.0 GHz

tasks.name: T2 scene_edit (concrete partition) on S01
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Place one AP at the centroid at 2.5 m height, frequency 5.0 GHz, power 20 dBm. Coverage threshold -50 dBm.

Step 1 — Compute baseline coverage of the room as generated. Save the resulting RSS grid as coverage_map_before.npy and report numerical_metrics.coverage_pct_before in simulation_result.json.

Step 2 — Edit the scene: add a full-height interior wall at x=2.5 m splitting the room into two halves, with material `itu_concrete`. Recompute coverage with the SAME AP and the concrete partition now in place. Save the new RSS grid as coverage_map_after.npy and report numerical_metrics.coverage_pct_after AND numerical_metrics.coverage_delta_pp = coverage_pct_after − coverage_pct_before (signed).

⚠ CRITICAL: Use Sionna RT (RadioMapSolver). FSPL fallback DOES NOT model walls, so a partition would have ZERO effect under FSPL and your delta would be 0 → AUTOMATIC FAIL. The point of this task is to test that you can model wall attenuation. Even if sionna throws errors on the first try, retry / fix the scene XML / shrink the grid; do NOT fall back to FSPL.

The reference oracle checks: (i) both before/after present, (ii) delta = after − before within ±2 pp, (iii) sign matches edit (action=added → expect Δ ≤ +5 pp; concrete partition typically gives Δ between -30 and -55 pp).
tasks.distractor: Wrong: not recomputing after the edit just reports baseline twice. Right: write two simulations (before and after the added step) and report a non-zero delta.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect edit applied: add a full-height interior wall at x=2.5 m splitting the room into two halves, with material `itu_concrete`
expect coverage_pct_before and coverage_pct_after both reported

tasks.name: T3 RT→PHY QPSK BER on S01
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Place 1 TX at (1, 1, 2.5) m and 1 RX at (4, 3, 1.5) m. Operating frequency 2.4 GHz (WiFi-2.4 band), modulation QPSK, SNR = 10 dB.

Step 1 — Compute the channel impulse response (CIR) for the TX↔RX link via Sionna RT's PathSolver / Paths API. Do NOT fall back to analytical FSPL — the point is to test that you can extract a real multipath CIR. Use the sionna conda env if `import sionna` fails (see $RF_SIONNA_PY). Save:
  numerical_metrics.cir_path_count        : int, number of multipath components
  numerical_metrics.path_delays_ns        : list[float], multipath delays (ns)
  numerical_metrics.path_gains_db         : list[float], multipath gains (dB)

Step 2 — Simulate uncoded QPSK BER over that CIR at SNR=10 dB. Convolve symbols with the CIR (the multipath spreads symbols → ISI). Run ≥ 10000 symbols for statistical reliability.

⚠ BER definition: count BIT errors, not symbol errors. For QPSK use Gray-coded 2 bits/symbol, then BER = bit_errors / total_bits. Uncoded BER for any binary modulation is physically bounded by BER ∈ [0, 0.5]; anything > 0.5 means you reported SER instead of BER.

Save:
  numerical_metrics.ber                   : float ∈ [0, 0.5], simulated multipath BER
  numerical_metrics.ber_theoretical_awgn  : float, ideal AWGN baseline at the same SNR (use Q(√(2·γ)) = 0.5·erfc(√γ))
  numerical_metrics.snr_db                : 10

The reference oracle checks: (i) ber ∈ [AWGN floor, max(1.5·Rayleigh, 0.5)] — allows ISI-dominated regime but rejects > 0.5; (ii) ber_theoretical_awgn matches the analytical Q-function within 3×; (iii) ber > AWGN-floor (the multipath must DEGRADE not improve the link vs AWGN). AWGN-only fallbacks (ber = ber_theoretical_awgn exactly) will FAIL.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: reporting AWGN BER (ignoring multipath) at the same SNR. Right: convolve the symbols with the simulated CIR; expect ber to differ from ber_theoretical_awgn at SNR=10 dB.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect ber and ber_theoretical_awgn both reported at SNR=10 dB

tasks.name: C6 IRC + 28.0 GHz coverage on S01
tasks.prompt: Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf (room_type='office'). Add one or more windows on perimeter walls totaling at least 1.60 m² (8% of 20.0 m² floor area, per IRC §R303). Place one AP at the centroid. Compute coverage at 28.0 GHz. Report coverage_pct, irc_compliant (true/false), total_window_aperture_m2.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: putting a 'window' on an interior wall (not facing exterior) — IRC requires perimeter wall windows. Right: place windows on north/south/east/west perimeter walls only.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect all windows on perimeter walls
expect coverage_pct AND irc_compliant both reported

tasks.name: C7 2-cell PF scheduling on S01
tasks.prompt: Generate a 5 m × 4 m home office (drywall walls) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf. Deploy 2 cells (APs as base stations) at evenly-spaced positions, 3.5 GHz. Place 4 users uniformly. Run proportional-fair (PF) scheduling for 100 TTI. Report under simulation_result.json.numerical_metrics: per_user_avg_rate (length-4 list of non-negative floats, bps/Hz), mean_throughput_bps_hz = mean(per_user_avg_rate), fairness_index = Jain's = (Σr_i)² / (n · Σr_i²). The reference oracle re-derives Jain's from per_user_avg_rate[] and rejects results where reported fairness or mean throughput don't match (±0.05 / ±0.2 bps/Hz).
tasks.distractor: Wrong: simulating only one cell and treating each user separately. Right: run a multi-cell scheduler that distributes capacity across all 4 users with PF metric T^(1−α)/r.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT

tasks.name: T2 scene_edit (concrete partition) on S11
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 8 m × 4 m L-shaped home office + study (drywall walls (L-shape: long arm 6x4, short arm 4x3)) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf, one filing cabinet. Place one AP at the centroid at 2.5 m height, frequency 5.0 GHz, power 20 dBm. Coverage threshold -50 dBm.

assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT

tasks.name: T3 RT→PHY QPSK BER on S11
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 8 m × 4 m L-shaped home office + study (drywall walls (L-shape: long arm 6x4, short arm 4x3)) containing one desk, one office chair, one bookshelf, one filing cabinet. Place 1 TX at (1, 1, 2.5) m and 1 RX at (7, 3, 1.5) m. Operating frequency 2.4 GHz (WiFi-2.4 band), modulation QPSK, SNR = 12 dB.

Step 1 — Compute the channel impulse response (CIR) for the TX↔RX link via Sionna RT's PathSolver / Paths API. Do NOT fall back to analytical FSPL — the point is to test that you can extract a real multipath CIR. Use the sionna conda env if `import sionna` fails (see $RF_SIONNA_PY). Save:
  numerical_metrics.cir_path_count        : int, number of multipath components
  numerical_metrics.path_delays_ns        : list[float], multipath delays (ns)
  numerical_metrics.path_gains_db         : list[float], multipath gains (dB)

Step 2 — Simulate uncoded QPSK BER over that CIR at SNR=12 dB. Convolve symbols with the CIR (the multipath spreads symbols → ISI). Run ≥ 10000 symbols for statistical reliability.

⚠ BER definition: count BIT errors, not symbol errors. For QPSK use Gray-coded 2 bits/symbol, then BER = bit_errors / total_bits. Uncoded BER for any binary modulation is physically bounded by BER ∈ [0, 0.5]; anything > 0.5 means you reported SER instead of BER.

Save:
  numerical_metrics.ber                   : float ∈ [0, 0.5], simulated multipath BER
  numerical_metrics.ber_theoretical_awgn  : float, ideal AWGN baseline at the same SNR (use Q(√(2·γ)) = 0.5·erfc(√γ))
  numerical_metrics.snr_db                : 12

The reference oracle checks: (i) ber ∈ [AWGN floor, max(1.5·Rayleigh, 0.5)] — allows ISI-dominated regime but rejects > 0.5; (ii) ber_theoretical_awgn matches the analytical Q-function within 3×; (iii) ber > AWGN-floor (the multipath must DEGRADE not improve the link vs AWGN). AWGN-only fallbacks (ber = ber_theoretical_awgn exactly) will FAIL.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: reporting AWGN BER (ignoring multipath) at the same SNR. Right: convolve the symbols with the simulated CIR; expect ber to differ from ber_theoretical_awgn at SNR=12 dB.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect ber and ber_theoretical_awgn both reported at SNR=12 dB

tasks.name: T3 RT→PHY QPSK BER on S14
tasks.prompt:
Generate a 8 m × 6 m Open-plan studio with half-height kitchenette partition (drywall walls + 1 half-height drywall partition (1.2 m tall) splitting living from kitchenette) containing one bed, one sofa, one kitchen counter, one dining table, one half-height partition. Place 1 TX at (1, 1, 2.5) m and 1 RX at (7, 5, 1.5) m. Operating frequency 2.4 GHz (WiFi-2.4 band), modulation QPSK, SNR = 12 dB.

Step 1 — Compute the channel impulse response (CIR) for the TX↔RX link via Sionna RT's PathSolver / Paths API. Do NOT fall back to analytical FSPL — the point is to test that you can extract a real multipath CIR. Use the sionna conda env if `import sionna` fails (see $RF_SIONNA_PY). Save:
  numerical_metrics.cir_path_count        : int, number of multipath components
  numerical_metrics.path_delays_ns        : list[float], multipath delays (ns)
  numerical_metrics.path_gains_db         : list[float], multipath gains (dB)

Step 2 — Simulate uncoded QPSK BER over that CIR at SNR=12 dB. Convolve symbols with the CIR (the multipath spreads symbols → ISI). Run ≥ 10000 symbols for statistical reliability.

⚠ BER definition: count BIT errors, not symbol errors. For QPSK use Gray-coded 2 bits/symbol, then BER = bit_errors / total_bits. Uncoded BER for any binary modulation is physically bounded by BER ∈ [0, 0.5]; anything > 0.5 means you reported SER instead of BER.

Save:
  numerical_metrics.ber                   : float ∈ [0, 0.5], simulated multipath BER
  numerical_metrics.ber_theoretical_awgn  : float, ideal AWGN baseline at the same SNR (use Q(√(2·γ)) = 0.5·erfc(√γ))
  numerical_metrics.snr_db                : 12

The reference oracle checks: (i) ber ∈ [AWGN floor, max(1.5·Rayleigh, 0.5)] — allows ISI-dominated regime but rejects > 0.5; (ii) ber_theoretical_awgn matches the analytical Q-function within 3×; (iii) ber > AWGN-floor (the multipath must DEGRADE not improve the link vs AWGN). AWGN-only fallbacks (ber = ber_theoretical_awgn exactly) will FAIL.
tasks.distractor: Wrong: reporting AWGN BER (ignoring multipath) at the same SNR. Right: convolve the symbols with the simulated CIR; expect ber to differ from ber_theoretical_awgn at SNR=12 dB.
assertions: must be loadable by Sionna RT
expect ber and ber_theoretical_awgn both reported at SNR=12 dB
